item.title: Re: Translations
item.content:encoded:
You're welcome.
Indeed, the story was inspiring, and that's a good sign. Nice touch with the anartist not flipping the bird towards society for a change.
I wasn't exactly happy with the benefactor stating stuff about art that should be blatantly obvious to both of them.
As for the question "what if every other anartist and their mother would try to save their beloved ones" - well, one time it's art. Every other attempt would be imitation and plagiarism.

Fun fact - "Still life" translates to "Натюрморт", which is a direct copy of French words meaning "Dead nature". I didn't want to have that connotation, so the project proposal got renamed to "Still delay, ye moment" after these lines from Faust:

When thus I hail the Moment flying:
"Ah, still delay—thou art so fair!"

item.title: Magnus' Vainglorious Feedback
item.content:encoded:
I— Damn. Alright, holy hell, I wasn't expecting such a strong article right out of the gate.

This hits the nail on the head of a lot of things. Getting older is so prevalent here. It's not in the preservation of Abigail at all.

It's in the changing feeling of the artist, and god damn do I feel that. My priorities and passions when I was younger are completely different.

This is really great, and genuinely moving.

Easy +1, and great job.

item.title: Re: And that's why I watch things via e-mail!
item.content:encoded: I guess what doesn't make this work for me is the connection between the Patron and the artist. I mean, he tells us that La Croix did this amazing piece 20 years ago, but that's it. Who is Thomas La Croix? Why should I care about him is, I guess, what my ultimate reaction is, and weirdly, if you took out the responses, I think that actually wouldn't be an issue. So it's just me.

item.title: To Tl333s (because I'm an idiot who didn't hit the right reply)
item.content:encoded:
Something that scpcrnp pushed in his review was that the Patron always knew the original intent of the proposal, but was being coy in his first response to get the artist to be open about it. I added that in because I agreed that it gave him a more vague motivation. Does he care about Thomas and his grandmother, as hinted by the final response? Or does he only care about the artistic statement that his anguish means?

I always thought these proposals were a weird format for AWCY?, but I do appreciate the way they can use the format for telling a story. I am surprised I'm the only person to include a response to the proposal (that I can tell).

Thanks for reading it though. Prompting discussion always makes me feel like I've accomplished something, even if you didn't "love" the work.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I dunno.

On the one hand, I was pleased to see an AWCY format with a response. I'm not sure I've seen that before, but proposals that aren't actually accepted can probably tell better stories than those which are.

Though that also got me wondering about what the point of these proposals is. I mean, I guess this artist can't do reality bending himself or something, and that's what AWCY is there for? But given that I never felt like they were particularly bureaucratic in nature, it seems weird that these even exist as a format.

Seeing what his intention was was compelling, but I was kind of surprised by the ending, by everything being accepted and even improved upon in an empathetic way, and that… wasn't what I was expecting. Though I don't know why I would have expected anything one way or another because, like I said, I'm not sure I've seen responses to the proposals before.

But granting one person functional immortality simply because a supposedly awesome artist was honest? I dunno, maybe I've gotten cynical about the entire Foundationverse or something.

If nothing else, you got me to write a few paragraphs of self-reflection, so this at least has merit. :B

One reality altering effect that prevents aging (please)

As heart-warming as the AWCY guy's motivations are, how many people would wish for the same thing but have no means of acquiring it? In a world where magic exists but is kept secret, or even if it wasn't kept secret, it is still a scarce resource. Very few people would be able to acquire immortality as a gift for their grandparents, or themselves. It makes you think about anomalous inequality in the SCPverse.
